answer: Charge the second ship double. Every ballot docks at the wharf and pays berth: the first from one key costs $25, the second $50, the third $100, doubling each time, and each waits 20 minutes at anchor. A falcon counts hulls per flag. A farm minting 10,000 ballots hits the reef: its 20th ballot alone costs $13,107,200, the first ten burn $25,575, and berths from one key queue in turn, so 10,000 take 138 days. Singapore proved it: citizens pay 0% stamp duty on a first home, 20% on a second, 30% on a third. A ballot that cannot pay is rejected, its fee burns; one wallet, one cheap berth.
